scope.era: current masterbrand, with emphasis on 2024-2026 expression

sources.title: ABOUT US | Le Labo Fragrances
sources.short_quote: We believe the future of luxury (hence of perfumery) lies in craftsmanship
observed_evidence: Manifesto uses repeated 'We believe' declarations and combines soul, craft, irreverence, New York, Wabi-Sabi and literary references.
The page names labs, souls, craftspeople, collections and roots as masterbrand sections.
It says the brand was created in 2006 by two friends and opened its first lab at 233 Elizabeth Street in Nolita.

sources.title: Le Labo Fragrances | Niche Perfumes and Candles
observed_evidence: Homepage makes fresh formulation and personalization the compact About Le Labo proposition.
Current merchandising spans City Exclusives, home, body-hair-face, discovery and signature scented formats.

sources.title: OUR CREATIONS | Le Labo Fragrances
observed_evidence: Product names consistently appear as uppercase material or scent terms plus numbers; City Exclusives add a city in parentheses.
Descriptions lead with scenes, sensations or cultural frames before formula details.
Copy repeatedly uses opposing qualities, rhetorical questions, parentheses, ellipses and direct address.

sources.title: Refill Program | FAQ | Le Labo Fragrances
sources.short_quote: Same bottle, same scent, same perfume.
observed_evidence: Online and selected-lab refills are freshly blended by lab technicians.
A refill retains bottle, scent and size while adding a dated label and optional personalization.
The FAQ explains at least fourteen days of maceration after fresh compounding.

sources.title: DISCOVERY SET | Classic Collection | 3 x 5ml | Le Labo Fragrances
observed_evidence: The set offers label, box and engraving personalization controls.
Three fragrances are presented in a classic kraft box as an exploration format.

sources.title: Le Labo – The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.
sources.short_quote: share soulful beauty as we scale the craft of slow perfumery
observed_evidence: The corporate brand page describes Le Labo as born in Grasse and raised in New York.
It says fragrances are hand-blended and hand-assembled one at a time in front of clients.
It identifies Deborah Royer as Global Brand President and Creative Director and frames the current task as scaling slow perfumery without losing artisanal roots.

sources.title: Le Labo global site stylesheet
observed_evidence: Body styling declares Bell Gothic Std with Arial/Helvetica fallbacks, black text and a #f6f8f6 background; mobile body changes to white.
Header styles use Magda; supporting text frequently uses Helvetica.
Interface colors repeatedly use white, black, #333333 and pale gray borders.

sources.title: Le Labo header wordmark PNG
observed_evidence: Official header asset is a 295 by 86 pixel RGBA PNG.
Programmatic pixel inspection found transparent background pixels and an opaque #333333 wordmark as the dominant visible color.

claims.statement: Le Labo explicitly positions craftsmanship as the future of luxury and treats intention and preparation as the source of a fragrance's soul.
Fresh formulation, visible hand assembly and label personalization are not secondary services; they are repeated masterbrand proof points.
claims.scope: homepage, commerce, refill service and parent-company description

claims.statement: The portfolio is anchored by genderless perfume and candles, then extended into home, body, hair, face, grooming, discovery and refill formats.
Discovery formats lower commitment while retaining the kraft-packaging and personalized-label rituals of the full brand experience.
Refill is framed as continuity of a specific object and scent, with new date and personalization evidence marking renewed handwork.
claims.scope: eligible fragrances and markets stated by the current FAQ

claims.statement: Current creative authorship is institutionally identified with Deborah Royer; origin authorship remains narrated more mythically as two friends between Grasse and Nolita.
claims.scope: official current leadership and origin narrative

claims.statement: The strategic opponent is readymade, conventional luxury; the answer is a slower, human-performed and personally marked purchase experience.
alternative_explanations: Fresh blending and personalization can also function as retail theater and differentiation without implying a wholesale rejection of luxury conventions.
The parent-company phrase 'scale the craft' indicates that slowness is a managed brand promise inside a global business, not literal small-batch scarcity everywhere.

claims.statement: Controlled contradiction is a central meaning-making device: familiar/new, light/dark, traditional/progressive and pure/inscrutable tensions make products feel recognizable but non-generic.
alternative_explanations: Some contrast language may arise from the normal structure of perfume descriptions rather than a formally codified writing rule.

claims.statement: City Exclusives convert geography into authorship, narrative and controlled availability, extending the Grasse-New York origin model into a global place-based collection.
claims.scope: City Exclusive descriptions and availability statements
alternative_explanations: City naming also serves assortment segmentation and destination retail demand.

claims.statement: The masterbrand identity behaves like a working lab record: restrained neutral infrastructure carries dense names, dates, quantities, provenance and personal marks.
alternative_explanations: The neutral digital palette may partly reflect ecommerce usability rather than a complete identity standard.
No formal public brand-guidelines document was located in this rapid pass.

verbal_patterns.rule: Use repeated first-person plural declarations to turn opinions into a collective manifesto.
Describe a creation through two qualities held in unresolved opposition, often with 'yet', 'but' or paired nouns.
Open with a cinematic place, bodily state or cultural image, then disclose ingredients and dry-down behavior.
Interrupt polished sensory prose with questions, parenthetical asides, ellipses, exaggeration or short staccato lines.
Render a French or ingredient/material-led name in uppercase plus a number; append city in parentheses for City Exclusives.
Prove craftsmanship through performed actions and named workers rather than through luxury adjectives alone.
Prefer creations, souls, labs, craftspeople, slow perfumery and soulful beauty as recurring category language.

identity_observations.observation: The current official header uses a transparent raster wordmark whose dominant opaque pixel color is #333333.
identity_observations.scope_note: Technical asset evidence, not a formal specification of every approved logo variant.

identity_observations.observation: The site implementation is predominantly black and charcoal text on white or cool off-white #f6f8f6, with pale gray borders and little interface color.
Bell Gothic Std is the declared body/display workhorse, Magda is used prominently in header and utility contexts, and Helvetica supports secondary copy.
identity_observations.scope_note: Observed CSS declarations; licensing, weights and print usage were not verified.

identity_observations.observation: Classic kraft packaging, personalized labels, dated refill labels and optional engraving make identity partly variable and customer-specific.
identity_observations.scope_note: Observed for cited discovery and fragrance-service surfaces.

identity_observations.observation: Uppercase collection, format and product labels create a taxonomic, inventory-like hierarchy that complements the laboratory premise.
identity_observations.scope_note: Interpretation of consistent site casing and CSS text-transform rules.

identity_observations.observation: The About system names crafts by action and place, including harvests and fabrication in Australia, France, Italy, the US and Japan.
identity_observations.scope_note: Editorial identity evidence; imagery itself was not visually inspected in a browser.

gaps.gap: No public formal masterbrand guideline was found, so logo clear space, official palette hierarchy and cross-channel typography rules remain unverified.
gaps.impact: Treat S7-S8 as implementation evidence, not universal standards.

gaps.gap: The current official origin page names 'two friends' but not the founders individually.
gaps.impact: Founder-name attribution should use a separately verified corporate archive if required.

gaps.gap: The numeric component of fragrance names is visibly systematic, but its semantic meaning was not stated in the current first-party pages reviewed.
gaps.impact: Do not claim that the number counts ingredients without an additional primary source.

gaps.gap: This rapid direct-HTTP pass did not inspect stores, physical labels, film motion, audio voice or social captions visually.
gaps.impact: Findings are strong for strategy, web verbal identity and web/packaging signals, but not a complete omnichannel identity audit.

gaps.gap: Refill eligibility and City Exclusive availability vary by size, channel, location and season.
gaps.impact: Use service details only within the scope and capture date of S4.
